# Crew — Project Roadmap

A living tracker for building the Crew multi-agent harness. The full design lives in [`PLAN.md`](./PLAN.md) (mirror of `~/.claude/plans/i-want-you-continue-golden-bonbon.md`).

**Repo root:** `~/Developer/ai-automation/` (this directory)
**Deployment target:** Mac mini (everything ships there once stable)
**Currently building from:** MacBook (planning + initial coding)

---

## Status at a glance

| Phase | State | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Plan** | ✅ approved | See `PLAN.md` |
| **Phase A — Crew repo scaffold** | ✅ complete | All 7 agents, 8 commands, templates, plists, Python skeleton in repo |
| **Phase B — Local validation on MacBook** | ⏭ superseded | Validated live on the Mac mini during Phase C; sandbox loop unnecessary |
| **Phase C — Mac mini provisioning** | ✅ complete | All 11 steps; bridge + scheduler live as launchd daemons |
| **Phase D — First project bootstrap (SMC)** | ✅ complete | D1+D3+D4+D5+D6 done. D2 deprecated 2026-05-15 (per-ticket scoping rolled back; see [[per-ticket-scoping-dropped]]). |
| **Phase D7 — Orchestration transparency** | ✅ complete | Tier 1 (JSONL events + bridge tailer); D7.5 Tier 2 deferred by design |
| **Phase D8 — Auto-scoping** | ⏭ rolled back | Module-reference logic stayed; per-ticket scope proposals removed 2026-05-15 |
| **Phase D9 — Per-project base branch** | ✅ complete | Long-form surface config with per-surface base_branch overrides |
| **Phase D10 — Per-hat dispatch** | ✅ complete | Bridge orchestrator owns chain; per-hat subprocess + abort visibility |
| **Phase D11 — Eager PR** | ✅ complete | @coder opens draft PR immediately; reviewer/qa post as PR comments |
| **Phase D12 — Linear SSOT** | ✅ complete | All hats post Linear comments; PR URL captured on ticket |
| **Phase D13 — Chat context** | ✅ complete | Last N Discord messages mounted as chat-context.md per dispatch |
| **Phase D14 — Meta commands** | ✅ complete | `[crew] /projects`, `/help`, `/status`, `/channels` |
| **Phase D15 — Bridge-routed scheduler triggers** | ✅ complete 2026-05-15 | Briefs slip the 9-min headless cap via the bridge owning the subprocess (25-min budget) |
| **Phase D16 — Multi-project briefs** | ✅ complete 2026-05-15 | Morning brief + evening digest walk every `projects.*` in config.yml |
| **Phase D17 — Per-bot model selection** | ✅ complete 2026-05-15 | `models:` block in config.yml; orchestrator/scheduler/bridge resolve per role |
| **Phase D18 — Integration auth monitoring** | ✅ complete 2026-05-15 | External heartbeat (claude/gh/op/bridge) every 30 min + MCP probe every 2h. Direct-to-Discord webhook fallback so a dead bridge still alerts. `[crew] /health` for on-demand view. |
| **Phase E — Pilot tickets** | ⬜ not started | First slot is FRO-237 per accepted roadmap |
| **Phase F — Fan out** | ⬜ not started | Remaining SMC backlog, then hustlrr |

---

## How to resume this project

If you (or a fresh Claude Code session) open this repo cold, do this:

1. **Read `PLAN.md` end-to-end.** Every architectural decision is there.
2. **Read `~/.claude/projects/-Users-rubenspessoa-Developer-ai-automation/memory/MEMORY.md`** for any feedback/preferences that shape how to work on this project.
3. **Check this ROADMAP for the current phase + last completed step.**
4. **Continue from the next unchecked item below.**

If you're on a fresh Mac mini that's never seen this project: follow `PLAN.md` → "Step-by-step setup runbook," starting at Step 1.

---

## Phase A — Crew repo scaffold (MacBook)  ✅

Goal: produce a complete, committable repo with all `.md` agent + command definitions, project templates, and Python skeleton.

- [x] **A1-A8** — All scaffold items delivered. Repo at `rubenspessoa/ai-automation`, cloned on Mac mini.

## Phase B — Local validation on MacBook  ⏭ superseded

Sandbox validation was folded into the live deployment on the Mac mini. The bridge E2E loop (2026-05-13) and `/work FRO-238` first-run validated the agent + command behavior on real systems. Strict sandbox loop deemed unnecessary; closing the phase.

## Phase C — Mac mini provisioning  ✅

- [x] **C1-C11** — All steps complete as of 2026-05-14. Bridge + scheduler live as launchd daemons (`launchctl list | grep crew`); iCloud backup running hourly; healthchecks.io pings wired per job.

## Phase D — First project bootstrap (SMC)

- [x] **D1** — `crew init` ran; `.crew/{architecture,ownership,voice}.md`, `.github/workflows/crew-ci.yml`, `.git/hooks/pre-commit` all present in `~/Developer/ai-plant-scanner/`.
- [⏭] **D2** — Per-ticket ownership.md scoping deprecated 2026-05-15. Per-ticket file-scope was redundant with Linear and added file-sync overhead with no defensive value once the lane system existed. Module-reference table stays in each project's `.crew/ownership.md` as repo-shaped documentation; lane label + architect/reviewer judgment + PR review do the gating. See `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/per_ticket_scoping_dropped.md`.
- [x] **D3** — Compiled `voice.md` in both SMC repos from `ai-plant-scanner-web/docs/copy-voice.md` (authoritative voice guide) + `src/lib/constants.ts` (brand anchors). 145-line iOS file + 143-line web file with: positioning sentence, brand anchors (name/tier/tagline/description), 4 voice pillars with do/don't examples, concision rules, banned strings (template defaults + SMC clichés), hard rules (no dashes, no excl marks except CTAs, smart quotes, numerals 2+), 7 "lines worth preserving", state-specific anchor patterns. Cross-references `copy-voice.md` as the canonical doc.
- [x] **D4** — SwiftLint rules tuned per `architecture.md` layer boundaries. `.swiftlint.yml` at iOS repo root validates clean: 7 custom rules (no_swiftui_in_domain, no_uikit_in_domain, no_appkit_in_domain, no_singletons_in_domain, no_views_in_data, no_naked_userdefaults_in_services, no_naked_urlsession_in_services) at error severity + hygiene rules (print(), TODOs without tickets) at warning. **architecture.md also rewritten** to match the actual flat-by-role layout (Services/Models/Views/etc.) rather than the template's nested-by-layer ideal. Live scan finds **2 real architectural errors in `SubscriptionService.swift`** that warrant their own Linear ticket; 60 style warnings are non-blocking.
- [x] **D5** — Test infrastructure in place in the IdentifierKit Swift package: `Package.swift` declares an `IdentifierKitTests` testTarget with `swift-snapshot-testing` (^1.17.0) as a test-only dep. Template tests written. `crew-ci.yml` extended with a `swift test --enable-code-coverage` step. **Verified 2026-05-15:** `swift test` runs end-to-end (36 tests, 7 suites pass). 5 snapshot baselines recorded under `Tests/IdentifierKitTests/Views/__Snapshots__/EntitlementGateModifierSnapshotTests/` (proLockedInDark, proLockedInLight, proSatisfiedRendersContent, requiresAccountLockedInDark, requiresAccountLockedInLight). Repo clean.
- [x] **D6** — Discord: `[SMC] @pm plan-roadmap` — first pass complete 2026-05-14. 22 tickets validated, 9 lane overrides applied (`lane:auto` → `lane:human-review`), 31 hustlrr tickets deferred. Sequence: FRO-237 → FRO-236 → FRO-265 → FRO-245 → FRO-239 → FRO-263. Saved at `~/.claude/agent-memory/pm/smc/roadmap.md`.

## Phase D7 — Orchestration transparency

Bridge currently captures only the final stdout of `/work` and posts it in the channel where the user typed. To support per-hat per-channel visibility (PM acks in `#pm-protagonist`, architect picks up in `#architect-design`, handoffs and push-backs announced as they happen), the bridge needs to read mid-workflow events.

Design lives in [[d7-transparency-design]] (memory). Three tiers; **Tier 1** is the recommended first iteration.

- [x] **D7.1** — `scripts/emit-event.py` writes structured events to `~/.crew/runs/<TASK>/events.jsonl`. CLI: `--task --channel --kind --text`. Validates channel ∈ {pm, architect, coder, reviewer, qa, echo, ledger, system} and kind ∈ {pickup, status, handoff, pushback, blocked, done}.
- [x] **D7.2** — Bridge spawns `_tail_events()` task per `/work` dispatch. Polls events.jsonl every 1 s, tracks byte position so each event lands exactly once. Posts to `discord.channels.<channel>` IDs from config.yml (`_load_channel_map()` coerces strings → ints once). Cancellation drains remaining events before exit.
- [x] **D7.3** — `commands/work.md` rewritten with explicit emission points: workflow start, before/after every hat, on handoff, push-back, loop-back, BLOCKED, completion (per-lane variants). Old "not wired in v1" note replaced with the live JSONL-tail design.
- [⏭] **D7.4** — Folded into D7.3: the workflow body is the emission point (it wraps every subagent invocation). Subagent definitions don't need their own emit calls in Tier 1.
- [ ] **D7.5** — Tier 2 (live per-hat status streams emitted from inside each hat) — defer until Tier 1 proves the model.

## Phase D10 — Per-hat dispatch (bridge becomes orchestrator)

Surfaced 2026-05-14 during the FRO-237 dry run. `/work` runs all hats inside a single `claude -p` invocation; the 28-min ceiling killed @reviewer + @qa + @pr after PM/architect/coder ate the whole budget. Full design in [[d10-per-hat-dispatch-design]].

Inverts the orchestration model: each hat is its own `claude -p` subprocess with its own ~28-min budget; the bridge holds the state machine and routes push-back/loop-back/BLOCKED transitions between hats.

- [x] **D10.1** — 6 per-hat command files written and symlinked into `~/.claude/commands/`: `work-pm.md` (brief.md production), `work-architect.md` (design.md + files.txt + concerns.md), `work-coder.md` (implementation + commit + draft PR via D11), `work-reviewer.md` (pre-PR review with findings as PR comments), `work-qa.md` (test + coverage gate per architecture.md taxonomy), `work-pr.md` (slim final hat — mark ready, auto-merge or sign-off). Each file: reads chat-context (D13), reads prior artifacts, does its work, posts Linear comment (D12), emits events, writes status.json with verdict. ~1200 lines total. Existing `commands/work.md` (mono-process) stays untouched as the D10.5 migration fallback until D10.2 lands.
- [x] **D10.2** — Bridge orchestrator at `crew/chat_bridge/orchestrator.py`. State machine over the hat chain; reads each hat's `status.json` to route DONE / PUSH_BACK / LOOP_BACK / BLOCKED. `main.py._dispatch` routes `slash_cmd == "work"` through it instead of the legacy mono path.
- [x] **D10.3** — `SessionDB.workflows` + `SessionDB.iterations` already existed from earlier scaffold; orchestrator uses `record_iteration` / `iteration_count` to enforce PUSH_BACK_CAP=2 and LOOP_BACK_CAP=3 across restarts.
- [x] **D10.4** — Orchestrator emits `handoff` (between successful DONE hats) and `pushback` (on push-back/loop routing) events directly to `events.jsonl`; per-hat command files emit only their own `pickup`/`done`/`status`. Clean ownership split.
- [x] **D10.5** — Mono path preserved: `main.py._dispatch` falls through to the legacy `_run_claude(prompt, ...)` for any non-`/work` slash command and any `/work` invocation where no TASK-ID is parseable. Effectively dormant for `/work` but available as a safety net.
- [✓] **D10.6** — Real-ticket validation merged into **Phase E1** (the first pilot). Phase D is the build; Phase E is the validate. No separate D10.6 step.
- [x] **D10.7** — Abort visibility implemented in `orchestrator._dispatch_hat` outcome handling: when a subprocess hits `TIMEOUT` / `CRASH` / `NO_STATUS`, the orchestrator synthesizes a `blocked` event for both `#system` and `#pm` channels via `_append_event` AND directly posts to those channels via `_post_to_channel` — so PM has immediate visibility even if the events tailer is between polls.

Depends on: D9 (base branch). Blocks: any non-dry-run pilot through Phase E.

## Phase D11 — Eager PR opening  ✅ 2026-05-14

Today's FRO-237 dry run committed 21 files but never opened a PR — `@pr` was the last hat and the chain died at @reviewer. Net effect: real code invisible outside the worktree path. See [[d11-eager-pr-design]].

- [x] **D11.1** — `commands/work-coder.md` DONE protocol includes `gh pr create --draft --base <default_base_branch>` + auto-generated body in `pr-body.md` pulling from brief.md + design.md + coder-notes.md. PR URL captured in `pr-url.txt`.
- [x] **D11.2** — `commands/work-reviewer.md` posts line-level findings via `gh api repos/.../pulls/<N>/comments` + summary via `gh pr review`. `review.md` kept as audit trail.
- [x] **D11.3** — `commands/work-qa.md` posts coverage + test results as PR comments + final status check (✅/❌).
- [x] **D11.4** — `commands/work-pr.md` reads PR status, flips draft → ready, enables auto-merge for `lane:auto` (`gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch`), emits sign-off-needed event for `lane:human-review`. Linear status flips to In Review.

All four sub-items implemented as part of D10.1's per-hat command file authoring.

## Phase D12 — Linear as the ticket SSOT  ✅ 2026-05-14

Today's run wrote brief.md / design.md / files.txt / concerns.md / coder-notes.md to `~/.crew/runs/FRO-237/` — substantive work invisible to anyone browsing Linear. The ticket page was only touched when @pm flipped status to In Progress. See [[d12-linear-ssot-design]].

- [x] **D12.1** — `commands/work-pm.md` Linear write section: scoping digest as a Linear comment (in-scope, out-of-scope, acceptance, key risks).
- [x] **D12.2** — `commands/work-architect.md` Linear write section: design summary + concerns digest with link to full design.md.
- [x] **D12.3** — `commands/work-coder.md` Linear write section: implementation digest with PR URL, files changed count, non-obvious decisions, deferred items.
- [x] **D12.4** — `commands/work-reviewer.md` + `commands/work-qa.md` post short Linear summary comments; detail lives in PR comments via `gh api`.
- [x] **D12.5** — `commands/work-pr.md` posts the final-status Linear comment + flips Linear ticket status to In Review.
- [x] **D12.6** — Hard rule in each command file: Linear-write failures degrade to a logged `status` event in events.jsonl; never block the workflow.

All six sub-items implemented as part of D10.1's per-hat command file authoring.

## Phase D13 — Chat-history context for hats

Every dispatch today starts amnesiac — claude sees only the current message body, no conversation history. PM and others can't reference earlier clarifications or scope amendments because they've never seen them. Discord is the right chat SSOT; pull N recent messages before each dispatch. See [[d13-chat-context-design]].

- [x] **D13.1** — `CrewBridge._capture_chat_context` async method: pulls last N messages from `message.channel.history` (filtered, ≤ 7 days, allowlist + bot only), writes markdown digest to either `~/.crew/runs/<TASK>/chat-context.md` (for `/work`) or `~/.crew/sessions/<channel>-chat-context.md` (for everything else).
- [x] **D13.2** — `CHAT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` map in `main.py`: `pm-chat`=30, `work`=15, `plan-roadmap`=30, `morning-brief`/`evening-digest`=50. Commands not in the map get no chat context.
- [x] **D13.3** — All 6 per-hat command files (from D10.1) already include "Setup step 0: read chat-context.md if present"; `pm-chat.md` and `plan-roadmap.md` updated to do the same against their session-scoped path.
- [x] **D13.4** — Filter: only messages from allowlisted users + the bot, `default` or `reply` MessageType, ≤ `CHAT_CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (7 days), non-empty `clean_content`. Triggering message excluded via `before=message`.

Depends on: D10.1 (per-hat command files are the natural place to wire step 0). Doesn't block D10/D11/D12, but adds depth to the per-hat experience once they land.

## Phase D14 — Meta commands (`[crew]` tag)

There's no way to list registered projects, discover available commands, or check what workflows are running. Friction grows once hustlrr onboards. Add a `[crew]` meta-tag for system-level commands. See [[d14-meta-commands-design]].

- [x] **D14.1** — Bridge routing: `_on_message` checks `project == "crew"` after tag extraction and routes to `_dispatch_meta(body)` instead of project-aware dispatch. No claude subprocess spawn for meta commands — handled directly in Python.
- [x] **D14.2** — `[crew] /projects` lists registered projects from `~/.crew/config.yml`: tag, name, surfaces (multi or single), Linear team + project, `default_base_branch`. Usage hints appended.
- [x] **D14.3** — `[crew] /help` lists meta commands + per-project commands with short descriptions and the tag-required reminder.
- [x] **D14.4** — `[crew] /status` reads `SessionDB.active_workflows()` + scans `~/.crew/runs/` for the 10 most recent run dirs, showing the last event timestamp for each.
- [x] **D14.5** — `[crew] /channels` lists `discord.channels.*` from config with the live Discord channel name + ID.

## Phase D9 — Per-project base-branch config  ✅ 2026-05-14

`/work` was rooting worktrees from whatever branch was checked out (effectively `main`), wrong for projects mid-migration. SMC's current state lives on `feat/save-my-cactus`. See [[smc-branching-strategy]].

- [x] **D9.1** — Added `default_base_branch` field to `~/.crew/config.yml` per-project schema; surface-level `base_branch` override supported via the long-form surface declaration. Fallback: `develop`, else `main`.
- [x] **D9.2** — `commands/work.md` step 7 rewritten: resolves base branch via 3-tier priority (surface override → project default → develop/main fallback), `git fetch`-then-`git rev-parse --verify origin/<branch>` gate, fail-closed with a clear error message, worktree creation uses `git worktree add ... origin/<base-branch>` so the resulting branch is correctly rooted.
- [x] **D9.3** — `feat/save-my-cactus` confirmed on origin at sha `a99ab6e5` (was already pushed — no MacBook action needed).
- [x] **D9.4** — `default_base_branch: feat/save-my-cactus` set for SMC in `~/.crew/config.yml`. Remove once develop re-baselines post-migration.

## Phase D8 — Auto-scoping during /plan-roadmap  ✅ 2026-05-14

Manual `ownership.md` maintenance doesn't scale past the first pilot — every ticket would need a hand-drafted glob set before `/work` can run on it. Moved scoping into `/plan-roadmap` so it happens once per ticket alongside lane assignment.

Design in [[d8-auto-scoping-design]] (memory).

- [x] **D8.1** — `agents/pm.md` updated: `/plan-roadmap` lifecycle mode now proposes a glob set per ticket, drawn from the ticket description + the project's `.crew/ownership.md` "Module reference" table. Hard rule: never invent globs outside the module map; flag `KNOWN UNKNOWN — needs module-map extension` when nothing fits.
- [x] **D8.2** — `commands/plan-roadmap.md` rewritten: the proposal block renders lane, surface, scope (with `why-lane` / `why-scope` justifications) per ticket. On `accept`, PM writes Linear labels AND scope rows to `.crew/ownership.md` (one commit per /plan-roadmap accept). New override grammar `override FRO-X scope: <new-globs>`.
- [✓] **D8.3** — Contract documented in `commands/plan-roadmap.md` "Hard rules" (architect push-back at /work writes a scope diff to concerns.md; PM updates ownership.md; workflow resumes). **Implementation** of the push-back routing happens as part of D10's bridge orchestrator.
- [✓] **D8.4** — Fail-closed behavior already in place (current `/work` aborts BLOCKED if no row exists). Preserved as the safety net.
- [x] **D8.5** — `agents/pm.md` morning brief format extended: each batch ticket gets a `[scoped ✓]` / `[scoped ⚠️ stale]` / `[scoped ✗]` badge plus a "Scoping health" summary section. Stale = globs reference paths that no longer exist in the current surface tree.

## Phase E — Pilot tickets

Sequence per the accepted roadmap. Each ticket exercises the full chain end-to-end through the deployed bridge.

- [ ] **E1** — `[SMC] /work FRO-237` (EntitlementState foundation — `lane:human-review`, surface:ios). Foundation for every Wave 1+ ticket.
- [ ] **E2** — `[SMC] /work FRO-236` (Component gap audit — High, surface:ios). Read-only audit; parallel-safe with E1.
- [ ] **E3** — `[SMC] /work FRO-265` (Community waitlist endpoint — surface:web). Cross-surface parallel.
- [ ] **E4** — Tune iteration caps, cost ceilings, proactive thresholds based on what we observed.
- [ ] **E5** — Subscription-billing audit (Claude Code usage reflects activity; API console shows zero).

## Phase F — Fan out

- [ ] **F1** — Run remaining SMC `lane:auto` tickets in parallel batches.
- [ ] **F2** — Handle `lane:human-review` tickets with sign-off flow.
- [ ] **F3** — Onboard hustlrr (separate Linear project on the FRO team — see [[linear-structure]]): `crew init`, register in config.yml, run `/plan-roadmap hustlrr`, pilot first ticket.
- [ ] **F4** — Onboard next product if/when one's ready.
- [ ] **F5** — Decide on v2 additions: @operative (when shipping volume justifies), @temporal (only if you start missing it), WIP > 3, auto-pickup of Ready tickets, etc.

---

## Decision log (for future-you)

Key choices made during planning, with rationale. See `PLAN.md` for the full version.

- **Foundation:** Claude Code native (subagents + slash commands + agent-memory). NOT OpenClaw (dead on Pro/Max since 2026-04-04 policy).
- **All LLM calls subscription-only** via `claude` CLI. Hard CI gate against `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- **Coding workflows = one Claude Code session** per ticket (sidesteps headless token-refresh bug). Briefings = cron-triggered `claude -p` under 10 min.
- **Discord MCP** for outbound; thin Python chat bridge for inbound.
- **WIP = 3** concurrent coding workflows; each in its own git worktree.
- **Linear as source of truth.** PM owns all state transitions via Linear MCP.
- **Daily loop:** PM proposes morning batch → you approve → bots run continuously within the batch → evening digest. Batch overflow policy `ask` (PM proposes more, you decide).
- **Push-back protocol:** Architect can push back to PM, Coder to Architect, Reviewer/QA to Architect. Each writes `concerns.md`. Cap of 2 push-backs per hat.
- **Urgent work:** new parallel Claude Code session, never preempts.
- **Three lanes:** `lane:auto` (bot owns end-to-end), `lane:human-review` (bot ships, you sign off), `lane:human-led` (bot scaffolds only, you code).
- **Clean Architecture mandatory** per project (`.crew/architecture.md`); 100% line coverage gate on `Domain/` files.
- **Reliability stack:** iCloud Drive hourly snapshot of state.db (via `sqlite3 .backup`) + agent-memory tarball; 1Password CLI; healthchecks.io; launchd with absolute paths. (Earlier draft: Litestream + restic → B2 — replaced 2026-05-13 because Linear+GitHub already hold the authoritative state and one provider is enough for a solo operator.)
- **Agents in v1:** PM, Echo, Ledger + 4 coding hats. @temporal and @operative deferred until they earn their slot.

+---
+description: Probe every Crew MCP integration with a minimal tool call. Detects MCP-level auth failures (Linear, GitHub, RevenueCat, Sentry, PostHog, App Store Connect). Posts a state-change alert to #system-alerts.
+---
+
+# /healthcheck-mcps
+
+You have been invoked to probe each Crew MCP integration. MCPs can only be exercised inside a `claude -p` session, which is why this is a slash command rather than a plain script. Keep it cheap — one minimal tool call per MCP.
+
+## Probes (one per MCP, in order)
+
+Run each tool call below. For each, record the result as `ok` (returned data) or `broken` (errored, timed out, or returned an auth-shaped failure). Don't retry on failure — once is enough for a healthcheck.
+
+1. **Linear MCP** — `mcp__linear__list_teams` with `limit: 1`
+2. **GitHub** — `gh api user --jq .login` via Bash (the gh CLI is what coding hats use; treat it as an integration)
+3. **RevenueCat MCP** — `mcp__revenuecat__list-projects` with `limit: 1`

description: Probe every Crew MCP integration with a minimal tool call. Detects MCP-level auth failures (Linear, GitHub, RevenueCat, Sentry, PostHog, App Store Connect). Posts a state-change alert to #system-alerts.
---

# /healthcheck-mcps

You have been invoked to probe each Crew MCP integration. MCPs can only be exercised inside a `claude -p` session, which is why this is a slash command rather than a plain script. Keep it cheap — one minimal tool call per MCP.

## Probes (one per MCP, in order)

Run each tool call below. For each, record the result as `ok` (returned data) or `broken` (errored, timed out, or returned an auth-shaped failure). Don't retry on failure — once is enough for a healthcheck.

1. **Linear MCP** — `mcp__linear__list_teams` with `limit: 1`
2. **GitHub** — `gh api user --jq .login` via Bash (the gh CLI is what coding hats use; treat it as an integration)
3. **RevenueCat MCP** — `mcp__revenuecat__list-projects` with `limit: 1`
4. **Sentry MCP** — `mcp__sentry__find_organizations`
5. **PostHog MCP** — `mcp__posthog__organization` (any single-org call)
6. **App Store Connect** — if `mcp__app_store_connect__*` is registered, attempt a minimal `list_apps`. If the MCP isn't registered, mark `not_configured` (different from `broken`).

For each probe, capture:
- `status`: `"ok"`, `"broken"`, or `"not_configured"`
- `error`: error message excerpt if broken (≤200 chars)

## Write the result

Write `~/.crew/health-mcps.json`:

```json
{
  "last_check_ts": "<ISO-8601 UTC>",
  "mcps": {
    "linear":        {"status": "ok",     "error": null},
    "github":        {"status": "ok",     "error": null},
    "revenuecat":    {"status": "broken", "error": "RC API key expired"},
    "sentry":        {"status": "ok",     "error": null},
    "posthog":       {"status": "ok",     "error": null},
    "app_store_connect": {"status": "not_configured", "error": null}
  }
}
```

## State-change alerting

Read the previous `~/.crew/health-mcps.json` (if it exists) before running probes. After probing:

- For each MCP that transitioned from `ok` → `broken` (or `not_configured` → `broken`), POST to `http://127.0.0.1:7878/alert`:
  ```json
  {"channel": "system", "level": "error",
   "text": "**<mcp>** MCP went broken — `<error excerpt>`. Refresh auth in 1Password + reload bridge."}
  ```
- For each MCP that transitioned from `broken` → `ok`, POST level `"info"`:
  ```json
  {"channel": "system", "level": "info",
   "text": "**<mcp>** MCP recovered."}
  ```
- No alert on steady state.

## Hard rules

- Subscription invariant — all LLM use happens via this `claude -p` session.
- Keep probes **minimal**: 1 trivial tool call per MCP. The point is to verify auth + reachability, not to exercise functionality.
- Do not retry. A flake is just a flake; we'll catch it next time. False-positive alerts erode trust faster than missed alerts here.
- If the bridge `/alert` endpoint is unreachable, log the alert into stdout (so the runner.py output captures it) and continue. Don't crash the probe.

"""Discord chat bridge daemon.

Long-running launchd LaunchAgent. Listens for Discord messages, allowlist-checks
the sender, maps channel/thread to a project + Claude Code session, and invokes
the appropriate slash command via `claude` CLI.

NEVER imports anthropic SDK — every LLM call is a `claude` subprocess that uses
~/.claude/auth OAuth from macOS Keychain (subscription billing).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

# discord.py is the standard library; left as a forward ref to keep the module
# importable on environments that haven't sync'd yet.
try:
    import discord  # type: ignore[import]
except ImportError:
    discord = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

import aiohttp.web
import structlog
import yaml

from crew import config as crew_config
from crew.chat_bridge import orchestrator
from crew.chat_bridge.allowlist import is_allowed
from crew.chat_bridge.routing import infer_project, route_command
from crew.chat_bridge.session_db import SessionDB

# Discord caps message bodies at 2000 chars. Keep some headroom for the
# `[project] ` prefix and the truncation suffix.
DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT = 2000
DISPATCH_CHUNK = 1900

# Per-slash-command dispatch timeouts. `claude -p` has a known headless
# token-refresh bug around 10-15 min (PLAN.md §What battle-testing changed §2),
# so anything that needs to run longer than that should use a different
# invocation path — but for now we keep all timeouts under the cap and let
# the chain fail loudly if it bumps into it.
DEFAULT_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT = 600
DISPATCH_TIMEOUTS: dict[str, int] = {
    "pm-chat": 600,             # 10 min — conversational, single-turn
    "plan-roadmap": 900,        # 15 min — backlog read + classify
    # morning-brief and evening-digest are bridge-routed from the scheduler
    # (via_bridge: true in jobs.yml) and synthesize portfolio-wide. 25-min
    # budget — same envelope as the /work hats, well above the historical
    # headless token-refresh threshold.
    "morning-brief": 1500,
    "evening-digest": 1500,
    "echo-scan": 600,
    "ledger-snapshot": 600,
    "address-pr-comments": 900,
    # /work runs the whole hat chain in one claude -p invocation via Task-tool
    # subagent dispatch. Capped just under the 30-min mark to leave headroom
    # for the bridge's reply-and-cleanup tail.
    "work": 1700,
    "status": 120,              # Fast — read SQLite, summarize
    # Cheap MCP probes; 5 min is plenty even with the slow ASC MCP.
    "healthcheck-mcps": 300,
}

# Scheduler-triggered slash commands (via POST /trigger). Map each to its home
# Discord channel name so the bridge knows where to post output. Anything not
# in this allowlist is refused — the trigger endpoint is not a generic /<any>
# escape hatch, only the long-running scheduled jobs that need to slip the
# 9-min runner cap.
TRIGGER_CHANNELS: dict[str, str] = {
    "morning-brief": "pm",
    "evening-digest": "pm",
    "echo-scan": "echo",
    "ledger-snapshot": "ledger",
    "address-pr-comments": "system",
    # Probes write health-mcps.json themselves and POST /alert on transitions;
    # post the stdout digest to #system for the steady-state visibility too.
    "healthcheck-mcps": "system",
}

TRIGGER_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
TRIGGER_PORT = int(os.environ.get("CREW_BRIDGE_TRIGGER_PORT", "7878"))

log = structlog.get_logger()

# Allow leading whitespace and any number of @-mentions (<@123>, <@!123>, <@&role>)
# before the project tag. Discord prepends mention tokens to message.content when
# the bot is pinged, and some clients add leading whitespace.
PROJECT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:<@[!&]?\d+>\s*)*\[([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\]\s*")

# Extract a ticket ID (e.g. FRO-237) from a dispatch body so we can locate the
# events.jsonl file for D7 orchestration transparency.
TICKET_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+)\b")

# Emoji prefix per event kind — shows up on each per-channel post.
EVENT_PREFIX = {
    "pickup": "🛠",
    "status": "💬",
    "handoff": "→",
    "pushback": "↩️",
    "blocked": "⚠️",
    "done": "✅",
}

# D13 — Discord chat-history window per slash command. Bridge fetches this many
# recent messages from the originating channel and writes them to chat-context.md
# before dispatching, so the workflow has conversational context.
CHAT_CONTEXT_WINDOW: dict[str, int] = {
    "pm-chat": 30,         # conversational; needs the most context
    "work": 15,            # workflow has its own scope; chat is supplemental
    "plan-roadmap": 30,    # planning conversation can sprawl
    "morning-brief": 50,   # overnight catch-up
    "evening-digest": 50,  # day's accumulated chat
}
CHAT_CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7


class CrewBridge(discord.Client if discord else object):  # type: ignore[misc]
    """Discord client that bridges to Claude Code."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        if discord is None:
            raise RuntimeError("discord.py not installed; `uv sync` first")
        intents = discord.Intents.default()
        intents.message_content = True
        super().__init__(intents=intents)
        self.sessions = SessionDB(Path.home() / ".crew" / "state.db")

    async def on_ready(self) -> None:
        log.info("bridge.ready", user=str(self.user))
        # Start the local trigger server alongside Discord login. Idempotent —
        # if Discord reconnects (on_ready fires again), the second call is a
        # no-op because aiohttp.TCPSite refuses to rebind.
        if getattr(self, "_trigger_runner", None) is None:
            await self._start_trigger_server()

    async def _start_trigger_server(self) -> None:
        """Bind the localhost trigger endpoint. Scheduler POSTs here to slip
        the 9-min headless cap for long-running scheduled jobs.

        Also exposes `/alert` so the scheduler (and any other local process)
        can have the bridge surface an auth or health problem to a Discord
        channel without spawning claude. No-claude alert path lets us flag
        token expiry, MCP 401s, exec failures, etc."""
        app = aiohttp.web.Application()
        app.router.add_post("/trigger", self._handle_trigger)
        app.router.add_post("/alert", self._handle_alert)
        app.router.add_get("/health", self._handle_health)
        runner = aiohttp.web.AppRunner(app)
        await runner.setup()
        site = aiohttp.web.TCPSite(runner, TRIGGER_HOST, TRIGGER_PORT)
        try:
            await site.start()
        except OSError as e:
            log.error("bridge.trigger_bind_failed", host=TRIGGER_HOST, port=TRIGGER_PORT, error=str(e))
            return
        self._trigger_runner = runner
        log.info("bridge.trigger_listening", host=TRIGGER_HOST, port=TRIGGER_PORT)

    async def _handle_health(self, request: aiohttp.web.Request) -> aiohttp.web.Response:
        return aiohttp.web.json_response({"ok": True, "user": str(self.user) if self.user else None})

    async def _handle_alert(self, request: aiohttp.web.Request) -> aiohttp.web.Response:
        """POST /alert — post a one-liner to a Discord channel without
        spawning claude. Used by the scheduler + heartbeat to surface auth /
        health failures.

        Body (JSON): {
            "channel": "system",          # required, must be in channel_map()
            "text":    "claude OAuth 401 — refresh CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN",
            "level":   "error" | "warn" | "info"   # optional, prefixes emoji
        }
        """
        try:
            payload = await request.json()
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, aiohttp.web.HTTPException) as e:
            return aiohttp.web.json_response({"error": f"invalid JSON: {e}"}, status=400)

        channel_name = str(payload.get("channel") or "system")
        text = str(payload.get("text") or "").strip()
        level = str(payload.get("level") or "info").lower()
        if not text:
            return aiohttp.web.json_response({"error": "text is required"}, status=400)

        channel_id = crew_config.channel_map().get(channel_name)
        if channel_id is None:
            return aiohttp.web.json_response(
                {"error": f"no Discord channel mapped for '{channel_name}'"},
                status=500,
            )

        emoji = {"error": "🚨", "warn": "⚠️", "info": "💬"}.get(level, "💬")
        body = f"{emoji} **bridge alert** · {text}"
        if len(body) > DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT:
            body = body[: DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT - 20] + "\n…(truncated)"

        channel = self.get_channel(channel_id)
        if channel is None:
            log.error("bridge.alert_channel_missing", channel=channel_name)
            return aiohttp.web.json_response(
                {"error": f"channel id {channel_id} not in cache"}, status=500
            )

        try:
            await channel.send(body)
        except Exception as e:
            log.error("bridge.alert_post_failed", error=str(e))
            return aiohttp.web.json_response({"error": str(e)}, status=500)

        log.info("bridge.alert_posted", channel=channel_name, level=level)
        return aiohttp.web.json_response({"posted": True})

    async def _handle_trigger(self, request: aiohttp.web.Request) -> aiohttp.web.Response:
        """POST /trigger — dispatch a scheduled slash command through the bridge.

        Body (JSON): {
            "slash_cmd": "morning-brief",     # required, must be in TRIGGER_CHANNELS
            "project":   "crew",              # optional, used for cwd resolution
            "body":      "extra args",        # optional, appended to "/<slash_cmd>"
            "timeout":   1500,                # optional, override default
            "model":     "opus"               # optional, override resolved model
        }

        The bridge spawns `claude -p` with the configured timeout (well above
        the scheduler's 9-min wall-clock), captures stdout, and posts it to
        the slash_cmd's home Discord channel from TRIGGER_CHANNELS.
        """
        try:
            payload = await request.json()
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, aiohttp.web.HTTPException) as e:
            return aiohttp.web.json_response(
                {"error": f"invalid JSON: {e}"}, status=400
            )

        slash_cmd = str(payload.get("slash_cmd", "")).lstrip("/")
        if slash_cmd not in TRIGGER_CHANNELS:
            return aiohttp.web.json_response(
                {"error": f"slash_cmd '{slash_cmd}' not in trigger allowlist"},
                status=400,
            )

        project = str(payload.get("project") or "crew")
        body = str(payload.get("body") or "")
        timeout = int(payload.get("timeout") or DISPATCH_TIMEOUTS.get(slash_cmd, DEFAULT_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT))
        model = payload.get("model") or crew_config.resolve_model(slash_cmd)

        channel_name = TRIGGER_CHANNELS[slash_cmd]
        channel_id = crew_config.channel_map().get(channel_name)
        if channel_id is None:
            return aiohttp.web.json_response(
                {"error": f"no Discord channel mapped for '{channel_name}'"},
                status=500,
            )

        cwd = _project_cwd(project) if project != "crew" else Path.home()
        prompt = f"/{slash_cmd} {body}".strip()
        env = {**os.environ, "CREW_PROJECT_TAG": project}

        log.info(
            "bridge.trigger_dispatch",
            slash_cmd=slash_cmd,
            project=project,
            channel=channel_name,
            timeout_s=timeout,
            model=model,
        )

        # Run the dispatch in the background so the POST returns fast — the
        # scheduler doesn't need to hold the connection open for 25 min.
        asyncio.create_task(
            self._trigger_run_and_post(
                slash_cmd=slash_cmd,
                prompt=prompt,
                cwd=cwd,
                env=env,
                timeout=timeout,
                model=model,
                channel_id=channel_id,
            )
        )
        return aiohttp.web.json_response({"accepted": True, "slash_cmd": slash_cmd})

    async def _trigger_run_and_post(
        self,
        *,
        slash_cmd: str,
        prompt: str,
        cwd: Path,
        env: dict[str, str],
        timeout: int,
        model: str | None,
        channel_id: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Background worker for the trigger endpoint. Spawns claude, posts result."""
        try:
            output = await _run_claude(prompt, cwd, env, timeout, model=model)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            log.warning("bridge.trigger_timeout", slash_cmd=slash_cmd, timeout_s=timeout)
            output = f"⚠️ `/{slash_cmd}` exceeded {timeout // 60}-min cap; aborted."
        except FileNotFoundError:
            log.error("bridge.trigger_no_claude", slash_cmd=slash_cmd)
            output = f"⚠️ `claude` CLI not on PATH; `/{slash_cmd}` could not run."
        except Exception as e:
            log.error("bridge.trigger_exception", slash_cmd=slash_cmd, error=str(e))
            output = f"⚠️ `/{slash_cmd}` crashed: {e}"

        channel = self.get_channel(channel_id)
        if channel is None:
            log.error("bridge.trigger_channel_missing", channel_id=channel_id, slash_cmd=slash_cmd)
            return

        body = output or f"_(`/{slash_cmd}` returned no output)_"
        try:
            # Chunk to Discord's 2000-char limit.
            if len(body) <= DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT:
                await channel.send(body)
                return
            remaining = body
            while remaining:
                if len(remaining) <= DISPATCH_CHUNK:
                    await channel.send(remaining)
                    return
                cut = remaining.rfind("\n\n", 0, DISPATCH_CHUNK)
                if cut == -1:
                    cut = remaining.rfind("\n", 0, DISPATCH_CHUNK)
                if cut == -1 or cut < DISPATCH_CHUNK // 2:
                    cut = DISPATCH_CHUNK
                await channel.send(remaining[:cut])
                remaining = remaining[cut:].lstrip()
        except Exception as e:
            log.error("bridge.trigger_post_failed", slash_cmd=slash_cmd, error=str(e))

    async def on_message(self, message: discord.Message) -> None:  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        # Ignore self
        if message.author == self.user:
            return

        # Allowlist
        if not is_allowed(message.author.id):
            log.warning("bridge.denied", user_id=message.author.id)
            return

        # Extract project tag
        match = PROJECT_TAG_RE.match(message.content)
        if not match:
            # Log the raw content so the failure mode is debuggable next time —
            # repr() makes mentions, escapes, and whitespace visible.
            log.warning(
                "bridge.tag_missing",
                user_id=message.author.id,
                raw=repr(message.content[:120]),
            )
            await message.reply("⚠️ messages must start with a project tag like `[smc]`.")
            return
        project = match.group(1).lower()
        body = message.content[match.end() :].strip()

        # D14: [crew] meta-tag → system-level commands handled directly by the
        # bridge (no claude -p spawn). /projects, /help, /status, /channels.
        if project == "crew":
            try:
                await self._dispatch_meta(message, body)
            except Exception as e:
                log.error("bridge.meta_dispatch_failed", error=str(e))
                await message.reply(f"⚠️ meta command failed: {e}")
            return

        # Validate project
        if not infer_project(project, message.channel.id):
            await message.reply(f"⚠️ project `{project}` is not registered in `~/.crew/config.yml`.")
            return

        # Dispatch
        try:
            slash_cmd = route_command(body, message.channel.name)
            await self._dispatch(message, project, slash_cmd, body)
        except Exception as e:
            log.error("bridge.dispatch_failed", error=str(e))
            await message.reply(f"⚠️ couldn't dispatch: {e}")

    async def _dispatch(
        self, message: discord.Message, project: str, slash_cmd: str, body: str
    ) -> None:  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        """Spawn `claude -p` for the slash command, capture stdout, post to Discord.

        Single-shot per message for now — no `--resume` / session continuity. The
        session_db tracks workflow state; conversational continuity will land when
        we wire `--resume <claude-session-id>` keyed off the Discord thread.
        """
        cwd = _project_cwd(project)
        prompt = f"/{slash_cmd} {body}".strip()
        env = {
            **os.environ,
            "CREW_INCOMING_MESSAGE": body,
            "CREW_PROJECT_TAG": project,
        }
        timeout = DISPATCH_TIMEOUTS.get(slash_cmd, DEFAULT_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT)

        # User-visible "working" state. Skip the ack reply for short commands
        # (status, pm-chat) — they return fast enough that two messages would
        # just be noise. The reaction goes on every dispatch since it's free.
        is_long = timeout > 60
        await self._react(message, "⏳")
        if is_long:
            await message.reply(
                f"🛠️ working on `/{slash_cmd}` — up to {timeout // 60} min."
            )

        log.info(
            "bridge.dispatch",
            project=project,
            slash_cmd=slash_cmd,
            cwd=str(cwd),
            body_len=len(body),
            timeout_s=timeout,
        )

        # D7 Tier 1: per-hat-channel transparency.
        # For `/work TICKET-N`, spawn an async tailer that watches
        # ~/.crew/runs/<TICKET>/events.jsonl and posts each line to its
        # destination channel as the workflow emits them.
        tailer: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        task_id: str | None = None
        if slash_cmd == "work":
            task_id_match = TICKET_ID_RE.search(body)
            if task_id_match:
                task_id = task_id_match.group(1)
                events_path = Path.home() / ".crew" / "runs" / task_id / "events.jsonl"
                tailer = asyncio.create_task(
                    self._tail_events(events_path, task_id, project)
                )

        # D13: capture chat context so the workflow sees prior conversation.
        # /work writes to the run dir so it survives across per-hat hats;
        # everything else writes to a session-scoped file under ~/.crew/sessions/.
        n = CHAT_CONTEXT_WINDOW.get(slash_cmd, 0)
        if n > 0:
            if slash_cmd == "work" and task_id is not None:
                chat_path = Path.home() / ".crew" / "runs" / task_id / "chat-context.md"
            else:
                channel_name = getattr(message.channel, "name", "unknown")
                chat_path = (
                    Path.home() / ".crew" / "sessions" / f"{channel_name}-chat-context.md"
                )
            await self._capture_chat_context(message, chat_path, n)

        # D10.2: /work now routes through the orchestrator instead of
        # one big claude -p. Each hat is its own subprocess with its own
        # ~28-min budget. The legacy mono path is preserved for every
        # other slash command and as a future fallback.
        if slash_cmd == "work" and task_id is not None:
            try:
                await orchestrator.run_chain(
                    bridge=self,
                    project=project,
                    task_id=task_id,
                    cwd=cwd,
                    env=env,
                    sessions=self.sessions,
                )
            except Exception as e:
                log.error("bridge.orchestrator_failed", task=task_id, error=str(e))
                await self._react(message, "❌", remove="⏳")
                await message.reply(
                    f"⚠️ orchestrator crashed on `{task_id}`: {e}. "
                    f"See ~/.crew/logs/bridge.err.log + ~/.crew/runs/{task_id}/."
                )
                if tailer:
                    await self._stop_tailer(tailer)
                return

            if tailer:
                await self._stop_tailer(tailer)
            await self._react(message, "✅", remove="⏳")
            # Don't post a big stdout summary — the per-channel events have
            # already kept the human in the loop. A short confirmation in
            # the originating channel is enough.
            await message.reply(
                f"`/work {task_id}` orchestration complete. See per-channel "
                f"events for the full chain; run dir at `~/.crew/runs/{task_id}/`."
            )
            return

        # Legacy mono path for non-/work commands
        model = crew_config.resolve_model(slash_cmd)
        try:
            output = await _run_claude(prompt, cwd, env, timeout, model=model)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            log.warning("bridge.dispatch_timeout", project=project, slash_cmd=slash_cmd)
            if tailer:
                await self._stop_tailer(tailer)
            await self._react(message, "❌", remove="⏳")
            await message.reply(
                f"⚠️ `/{slash_cmd}` exceeded {timeout // 60}-min cap; aborted."
            )
            return
        except FileNotFoundError:
            if tailer:
                await self._stop_tailer(tailer)
            await self._react(message, "❌", remove="⏳")
            await message.reply("⚠️ `claude` CLI not on PATH for the bridge process.")
            return

        # Drain any events written between the last poll and subprocess exit
        # before cancelling the tailer.
        if tailer:
            await self._stop_tailer(tailer)

        await self._react(message, "✅", remove="⏳")
        await _post_chunked(message, output or "_(claude returned no output)_")

    async def _dispatch_meta(
        self,
        message: "discord.Message",  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        body: str,
    ) -> None:
        """D14 — handle `[crew] /<command>` system-level invocations.

        Supported: /projects, /help, /status, /channels. Anything else gets
        a usage hint pointing at /help.
        """
        cmd = body.lstrip("/").split()[0].lower() if body.startswith("/") else ""

        if cmd == "projects":
            await message.reply(self._format_projects())
        elif cmd == "help":
            await message.reply(self._format_help())
        elif cmd == "status":
            await message.reply(self._format_status())
        elif cmd == "channels":
            await message.reply(self._format_channels())
        elif cmd == "health":
            await message.reply(self._format_health())
        else:
            await message.reply(
                "Unknown `[crew]` command. Try `[crew] /help` to see what's available."
            )

    def _format_health(self) -> str:
        """Render ~/.crew/health.json (shell-level heartbeat) +
        ~/.crew/health-mcps.json (claude-side MCP probes) as a single
        on-demand status view. Read-only — no probe is triggered here.
        """
        lines = [
            f"**Crew · integration health · {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}**",
            "",
        ]

        def _emoji(status: str) -> str:
            return {"ok": "✅", "broken": "🚨", "not_configured": "➖"}.get(status, "❓")

        shell_path = Path.home() / ".crew" / "health.json"
        if shell_path.is_file():
            try:
                shell = json.loads(shell_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                lines.append("**Shell-level (heartbeat, runs every 30 min):**")
                ts = shell.get("last_check_ts", "?")
                lines.append(f"  _last probe: {ts}_")
                for name, entry in (shell.get("integrations") or {}).items():
                    status = entry.get("status", "?")
                    error = entry.get("last_error")
                    line = f"  {_emoji(status)} `{name}`"
                    if error:
                        line += f" — `{error[:120]}`"
                    lines.append(line)
                lines.append("")
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
                lines.append("_(health.json unreadable)_")
                lines.append("")
        else:
            lines.append("_Shell heartbeat hasn't written health.json yet._")
            lines.append("")

        mcp_path = Path.home() / ".crew" / "health-mcps.json"
        if mcp_path.is_file():
            try:
                mcps = json.loads(mcp_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                lines.append("**MCP-level (probe via claude, runs every 2h):**")
                ts = mcps.get("last_check_ts", "?")
                lines.append(f"  _last probe: {ts}_")
                for name, entry in (mcps.get("mcps") or {}).items():
                    status = entry.get("status", "?")
                    error = entry.get("error")
                    line = f"  {_emoji(status)} `{name}`"
                    if error:
                        line += f" — `{error[:120]}`"
                    lines.append(line)
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
                lines.append("_(health-mcps.json unreadable)_")
        else:
            lines.append("_MCP healthcheck hasn't written health-mcps.json yet._")

        return "\n".join(lines)

    def _format_projects(self) -> str:
        cfg = _load_config()
        projects = cfg.get("projects", {}) if isinstance(cfg, dict) else {}
        if not isinstance(projects, dict) or not projects:
            return (
                "Crew · registered projects · "
                f"{datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}\n\n"
                "_(no projects registered)_\n\n"
                "Add one to `~/.crew/config.yml` under `projects:` to see it here."
            )

        lines = [
            f"**Crew · registered projects · {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}**",
            "",
        ]
        for tag, entry in projects.items():
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            lines.append(f"**`{tag}`** — {entry.get('name', '?')}")
            # Surfaces
            if isinstance(entry.get("surfaces"), dict):
                for name, path in entry["surfaces"].items():
                    p = path if isinstance(path, str) else path.get("path", "?")
                    lines.append(f"  · surface `{name}` → `{p}`")
            elif isinstance(entry.get("repo"), str):
                lines.append(f"  · repo → `{entry['repo']}`")
            # Linear
            team = entry.get("linear_team", "?")
            proj = entry.get("linear_project", "?")
            lines.append(f"  · Linear: team `{team}` / project `{proj}`")
            # Base branch
            bb = entry.get("default_base_branch")
            if bb:
                lines.append(f"  · base branch: `{bb}`")
            lines.append("")

        lines.append("Usage:")
        lines.append("  `[<tag>] /work <TICKET>` — run the full workflow")
        lines.append("  `[<tag>] @pm <question>` — chat with PM")
        lines.append("  `[<tag>] /plan-roadmap` — (re-)classify the backlog")
        lines.append("  `[crew] /help` — list all commands")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def _format_status(self) -> str:
        active = []
        try:
            active = self.sessions.active_workflows()
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("bridge.status_db_failed", error=str(e))

        # Also scan ~/.crew/runs/ for any runs not in the DB (e.g. mono runs
        # from the legacy path, or runs that crashed before SessionDB recorded).
        runs_dir = Path.home() / ".crew" / "runs"
        recent_runs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []  # (ticket, last-event-ts)
        if runs_dir.is_dir():
            for run_path in sorted(runs_dir.iterdir(), reverse=True)[:10]:
                if not run_path.is_dir() or not run_path.name.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").replace(".", "").isalnum():
                    continue
                events_file = run_path / "events.jsonl"
                if events_file.is_file():
                    try:
                        last_line = events_file.read_text().strip().split("\n")[-1]
                        if last_line:
                            event = json.loads(last_line)
                            recent_runs.append((run_path.name, str(event.get("ts", "?"))))
                    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, IndexError):
                        pass

        lines = [
            f"**Crew · status · {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}**",
            "",
        ]
        if active:
            lines.append("**Active workflows (state.db):**")
            for w in active:
                lines.append(
                    f"  · `{w.get('ticket')}` ({w.get('project')}) "
                    f"state=`{w.get('state')}` branch=`{w.get('branch')}`"
                )
            lines.append("")
        else:
            lines.append("_No active workflows in state.db._")
            lines.append("")

        if recent_runs:
            lines.append("**Recent run dirs (last 10):**")
            for ticket, ts in recent_runs:
                lines.append(f"  · `{ticket}` — last event {ts}")
        return "\n".join(lines)[:1900]

    def _format_channels(self) -> str:
        channels = _load_channel_map()
        if not channels:
            return "_No channels configured in `~/.crew/config.yml` under `discord.channels`._"

        lines = [
            f"**Crew · Discord channels · {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}**",
            "",
        ]
        for name, cid in sorted(channels.items()):
            ch = self.get_channel(cid)
            label = f"#{ch.name}" if ch else "_(not cached)_"
            lines.append(f"  · `{name}` → {label} (`{cid}`)")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    async def _capture_chat_context(
        self,
        message: "discord.Message",  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        context_path: Path,
        n: int,
    ) -> None:
        """D13 — fetch last `n` messages from message.channel and write a markdown digest.

        Filtering (D13.4):
          - allowlisted authors only (from config.yml allowlist_user_ids + self.user)
          - messages newer than CHAT_CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_DAYS
          - skip system messages / pure-reaction-only messages
          - skip the triggering message itself (`before=message`)

        Output format: newest-last (chronological), one entry per message,
        author + ISO-8601 timestamp + `> body`. Hat commands have a Setup
        step 0 telling them to read this file if present.

        Best-effort: errors are logged but don't block dispatch.
        """
        try:
            from crew.chat_bridge.allowlist import _load_allowlist
            allowed_ids = set(_load_allowlist())
        except Exception:
            allowed_ids = set()
        if self.user is not None:
            allowed_ids.add(int(self.user.id))

        cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=CHAT_CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_DAYS)
        collected: list["discord.Message"] = []  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        try:
            async for m in message.channel.history(limit=n * 3, before=message):
                if int(m.author.id) not in allowed_ids:
                    continue
                if m.created_at < cutoff:
                    continue
                if m.type != discord.MessageType.default and m.type != discord.MessageType.reply:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                    continue
                content = (m.clean_content or "").strip()
                if not content:
                    continue
                collected.append(m)
                if len(collected) >= n:
                    break
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("bridge.chat_context_history_failed", error=str(e))
            return

        if not collected:
            log.info("bridge.chat_context_empty", path=str(context_path))
            return

        lines = [
            f"# Chat context (last {len(collected)} messages from #{getattr(message.channel, 'name', '?')})",
            "",
            "Format: `Author · ISO-8601 timestamp` then `> body`. Newest-last (chronological).",
            "",
        ]
        # Discord history() is newest-first; we want newest-last in the file.
        for m in reversed(collected):
            author = getattr(m.author, "display_name", str(m.author))
            lines.append("---")
            lines.append(f"**{author}** · {m.created_at.isoformat()}")
            # Indent body lines as a blockquote
            body = (m.clean_content or "").strip().replace("\n", "\n> ")
            lines.append(f"> {body}")
            lines.append("")

        try:
            context_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            context_path.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
            log.info(
                "bridge.chat_context_written",
                path=str(context_path),
                messages=len(collected),
            )
        except OSError as e:
            log.warning("bridge.chat_context_write_failed", error=str(e))

    async def _tail_events(
        self,
        events_path: Path,
        task_id: str,
        project: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Watch a workflow's events.jsonl and post each line to its target Discord channel.

        Polls the file every second. Tracks byte position so each event lands
        exactly once even if the file is appended-to mid-poll. Cancellation
        from the caller stops the loop cleanly.
        """
        channels = _load_channel_map()
        # Ensure the file exists so we can open it pre-emptively — the workflow
        # may not have created it yet when this task starts.
        events_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        events_path.touch(exist_ok=True)
        position = 0

        log.info("bridge.tail_start", task=task_id, path=str(events_path))
        try:
            while True:
                position = await self._drain_events(
                    events_path, position, channels, task_id, project
                )
                await asyncio.sleep(1)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # One last drain before exiting — catches anything written between
            # the last poll and subprocess completion.
            await self._drain_events(events_path, position, channels, task_id, project)
            log.info("bridge.tail_stop", task=task_id)
            raise

    async def _drain_events(
        self,
        events_path: Path,
        position: int,
        channels: dict[str, int],
        task_id: str,
        project: str,
    ) -> int:
        """Read new lines from `position` onward, post each, return the new position."""
        try:
            with events_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.seek(position)
                while True:
                    line = f.readline()
                    if not line:
                        return f.tell()
                    if not line.strip():
                        continue
                    try:
                        event = json.loads(line)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        log.warning("bridge.tail_bad_json", task=task_id, raw=line[:120])
                        continue
                    await self._post_event(event, channels, project)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return position

    async def _post_event(
        self,
        event: dict[str, object],
        channels: dict[str, int],
        project: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Look up the destination channel for one event and send the formatted line."""
        channel_name = str(event.get("channel") or "pm")
        kind = str(event.get("kind") or "status")
        text = str(event.get("text") or "")
        task = str(event.get("task") or "?")

        channel_id = channels.get(channel_name)
        if channel_id is None:
            log.warning("bridge.tail_unknown_channel", channel=channel_name, task=task)
            return

        channel = self.get_channel(channel_id)
        if channel is None:
            # Channel not in cache — try a fetch (network round-trip).
            try:
                channel = await self.fetch_channel(channel_id)
            except Exception as e:
                log.warning(
                    "bridge.tail_channel_fetch_failed",
                    channel_id=channel_id,
                    error=str(e),
                )
                return

        prefix = EVENT_PREFIX.get(kind, "·")
        body = f"[{project}] {prefix} **{task}** · {text}"
        try:
            await channel.send(body[:DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT])
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("bridge.tail_send_failed", error=str(e), task=task)

    async def _stop_tailer(self, tailer: asyncio.Task[None]) -> None:
        """Cancel an in-flight tailer and wait briefly for its final drain pass."""
        tailer.cancel()
        try:
            await tailer
        except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
            pass

    async def _react(
        self,
        message: "discord.Message",  # type: ignore[name-defined]
        emoji: str,
        remove: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Best-effort reaction toggle. Discord/network hiccups don't break dispatch."""
        try:
            if remove:
                await message.remove_reaction(remove, self.user)
            await message.add_reaction(emoji)
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("bridge.react_failed", emoji=emoji, error=str(e))

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _load_config() -> dict[str, object]:
    """Load ~/.crew/config.yml once, with caching. Returns {} if missing."""
    path = Path.home() / ".crew" / "config.yml"
    if not path.exists():
        return {}
    with path.open() as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}


def _load_channel_map() -> dict[str, int]:
    """Read discord.channels from ~/.crew/config.yml as {hat_name → channel_id_int}.

    Config stores channel IDs as strings; Discord's API wants ints. We coerce
    once here so callers don't have to. Unknown / non-numeric values are
    skipped with a log warning.
    """
    raw = _load_config().get("discord", {})
    channels = raw.get("channels", {}) if isinstance(raw, dict) else {}
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    if isinstance(channels, dict):
        for name, value in channels.items():
            try:
                out[str(name)] = int(str(value))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                log.warning("bridge.bad_channel_id", channel=name, value=str(value))
    return out


def _project_cwd(project: str) -> Path:
    """Pick a working directory for the slash command's `claude` invocation.

    Supports two surface shapes in `~/.crew/config.yml`:
      surfaces:
        ios: /path/to/repo                              # short form
        web:
          path: /path/to/repo                           # long form (allows
          base_branch: develop                          # per-surface base
                                                        # branch override)

    For single-surface projects, that's `projects.<id>.repo`. For multi-surface
    projects, the bridge picks the first registered surface as cwd; slash
    commands that need a specific surface (e.g. /work) re-resolve based on the
    Linear ticket's `surface:*` label.
    """
    cfg = _load_config().get("projects", {})
    if not isinstance(cfg, dict) or project not in cfg:
        return Path.home()  # fallback; claude can still run, just won't be in a project repo
    entry = cfg[project]
    if isinstance(entry, dict):
        if isinstance(entry.get("repo"), str):
            return Path(entry["repo"])
        surfaces = entry.get("surfaces")
        if isinstance(surfaces, dict) and surfaces:
            first = next(iter(surfaces.values()))
            # Short form: value is a path string
            if isinstance(first, str):
                return Path(first)
            # Long form: value is a dict with .path
            if isinstance(first, dict) and isinstance(first.get("path"), str):
                return Path(first["path"])
    return Path.home()


async def _run_claude(
    prompt: str,
    cwd: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    timeout: int,
    model: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Spawn `claude -p <prompt>` in `cwd`, capture stdout, return decoded string.

    If `model` is provided, splices `--model <model>` into the argv. Accepts
    aliases (``opus``/``sonnet``/``haiku``) or full IDs (``claude-opus-4-7``).
    Raises TimeoutError if it doesn't finish in `timeout` seconds. Stderr is
    logged but not surfaced to Discord unless the process failed entirely.
    """
    argv: list[str] = ["claude", "-p", prompt]
    if model:
        argv.extend(["--model", model])
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        *argv,
        cwd=str(cwd),
        env=env,
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    try:
        stdout_b, stderr_b = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=timeout)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        proc.kill()
        await proc.wait()
        raise

    stdout = stdout_b.decode(errors="replace").strip()
    stderr = stderr_b.decode(errors="replace").strip()
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        log.warning(
            "bridge.claude_nonzero",
            returncode=proc.returncode,
            stderr=stderr[:500],
        )
        # Surface the stderr so the user sees what went wrong rather than a silent fail.
        return f"_(claude exited {proc.returncode})_\n```\n{stderr[:1500]}\n```"
    if stderr:
        log.info("bridge.claude_stderr", stderr=stderr[:500])
    return stdout


async def _post_chunked(message: "discord.Message", body: str) -> None:  # type: ignore[name-defined]
    """Post `body` back to Discord, chunking to stay under the 2000-char limit."""
    if len(body) <= DISCORD_MSG_LIMIT:
        await message.reply(body)
        return
    # Split on paragraph boundaries where possible; fall back to hard chunks.
    parts: list[str] = []
    remaining = body
    while remaining:
        if len(remaining) <= DISPATCH_CHUNK:
            parts.append(remaining)
            break
        cut = remaining.rfind("\n\n", 0, DISPATCH_CHUNK)
        if cut == -1:
            cut = remaining.rfind("\n", 0, DISPATCH_CHUNK)
        if cut == -1 or cut < DISPATCH_CHUNK // 2:
            cut = DISPATCH_CHUNK
        parts.append(remaining[:cut])
        remaining = remaining[cut:].lstrip()
    first, *rest = parts
    sent = await message.reply(first)
    for part in rest:
        # Reply to the previous part keeps the thread linear and visually grouped.
        sent = await sent.reply(part)


def main() -> None:
    """Entrypoint — invoked by launchd via `op run` to inject DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN."""
    token = os.environ.get("DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        raise RuntimeError("DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN missing — run under `op run`")
    bridge = CrewBridge()
    bridge.run(token)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
